questions.question: Transform the simple sentence into a complex sentence: 'Hearing the alarming noise, the villagers woke up.'

options.text: The villagers heard the alarming noise and they woke up.

options.label: C

options.label: D
options.text: Having heard the noise, the villagers woke up.

questions.correct_answer_text: When the villagers heard the alarming noise, they woke up.
questions.explanation: A complex sentence contains one independent clause and at least one subordinate clause, introduced here by the conjunction 'When'.

questions.question: Transform into complex: 'In spite of working diligently, he failed to achieve his sales quota.'

options.label: A
options.text: Though he worked diligently, he failed to achieve his sales quota.

questions.correct_answer_text: Though he worked diligently, he failed to achieve his sales quota.
questions.explanation: The prepositional phrase 'In spite of' in a simple sentence transforms into a concessive adverbial clause introduced by 'Though / Although' in a complex sentence.

questions.question: Transform into complex: 'I saw a wounded bird lying on the grass.'

questions.explanation: An adjectival participle ('wounded bird') in a simple sentence transforms into an adjectival relative clause ('a bird that was wounded').

questions.question: Transform into complex: 'Tell me your date of birth.'

questions.question: Transform into complex: 'He is too feeble to walk without crutches.'

questions.explanation: 'Too... to...' in a simple sentence converts into 'so... that + subject + cannot...' in a complex sentence.

questions.question: Transform into a simple sentence: 'Since the weather was stormy, the fishermen did not sail out.'

questions.correct_answer_text: The weather being stormy, the fishermen did not sail out.
questions.explanation: A simple sentence contains exactly one finite verb; the causal subordinate clause with a different subject becomes a nominative absolute phrase ('The weather being stormy').

questions.question: Transform into simple: 'A man who is industrious is bound to prosper in life.'

questions.question: Transform into simple: 'We read newspapers so that we can keep abreast of current global affairs.'

questions.question: Transform into simple: 'Although she was fatigued, she continued her night shift.'

questions.explanation: The noun clause 'that he had made...' simplifies into a gerund phrase ('making a grave blunder') as the direct object.

questions.question: Transform into compound: 'Because of his chronic illness, he could not sit for the final exam.'
